result.title: Going Deeper With Memories
result.summary: Byte level language models avoid tokenizer dependence and provide universal coverage, but processing every byte at full resolution is expensive. We introduce DeepMem, a causal multiscale architecture that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation. A learned invertible subband transform constructs a hierarchy of shorter sequences, while a lossless carrier and explicit detail sidebands preserve byte identity. Fast weight memory blocks operate along the encoder, with iterative shared state computation at the compressed bottleneck, while an attention based super resolution decoder restores byte resolution representations. DeepMem achieves stronger language modeling performance than a matched byte level Transformer on FineWeb-Edu and PG19, and obtains the best macro average performance across the evaluated FLORES languages. It also improves PIQA accuracy while remaining competitive on code modeling, multiple choice reasoning, and byte level corruption robustness. Bottleneck refinement requires approximately $7{,}600\times$ fewer counted FLOPs than equivalent full resolution reasoning, while maintaining competitive evaluation throughput.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DeepMem，一种字节级语言模型的多尺度因果架构：用可逆子带变换构建短序列层级，并以无损载波与显式细节边带保留精确字节信息，在压缩瓶颈处迭代共享状态计算，再由注意力超分辨率解码器恢复字节级表示。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「语义压缩＋细节边带」的可逆多尺度设计可供核查 latent 推理中的视觉旁路与信息坍缩问题，瓶颈处迭代共享状态也可能迁移到压缩工作区的循环计算与动态算力分配。
